sections.label: Deferment of Kuala Lumpur-Singapore High Speed Rail
sections.summary: Singapore agreed to Malaysia's request to defer the Kuala Lumpur-Singapore High Speed Rail Project up to 31 May 2020, concluding a formal agreement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: A constructive and positive working relationship with our closest neighbour is also important for the region, and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) in particular, where Singapore and Malaysia have many shared interests.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: So, last August, when Malaysia sought Singapore’s agreement to defer the Kuala Lumpur-Singapore High Speed Rail Project up to 31 May 2020, we agreed to do so, and we concluded a formal agreement with Malaysia to achieve this deferment.

sections.label: Maritime and airspace issues with Malaysia
sections.summary: Two sets of difficult issues flared up: maritime issues over Malaysia's purported extension of Johor Bahru Port Limits, and airspace issues over Seletar Airport.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: In the past couple of months, two sets of difficult issues have flared up between Singapore and Malaysia.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: These include, first, the maritime issues surrounding Malaysia’s purported extension of the Johor Bahru Port Limits, and second, airspace issues arising from Malaysia's objections to the new Instrument Landing System (ILS) procedures for Seletar Airport, and its sudden promulgation of a permanent Restricted Area over Pasir Gudang, that disrupted normal operations at Seletar Airport which, in fact, have been conducted safely and efficiently for many decades.

sections.label: Envoys and meeting on outstanding issues
sections.summary: Prime Minister Lee sent special envoys to Prime Minister Mahathir, and the speaker met Malaysian Foreign Minister Saifuddin Abdullah to discuss outstanding issues.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: They created the risk of a dangerous downward spiral of measures and countermeasures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: They were serious enough that Prime Minister Lee felt it was necessary to send Deputy Prime Minister Teo Chee Hean and Minister Heng Swee Keat as special envoys to call on Prime Minister Mahathir on New Year's eve to convey a serious message from Prime Minister Lee expressing his grave concerns.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Arising from Prime Minister Lee’s communication with Prime Minister Mahathir, I met Malaysian Foreign Minister Saifuddin Abdullah last week to discuss these outstanding issues.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We agreed on measures to help keep the situation on the ground calm in order to allow discussions to take place in a more conducive atmosphere.

sections.label: Malaysia extends Johor Bahru Port Limits
sections.summary: On 25 October 2018, Malaysia unilaterally extended the Johor Bahru Port Limits into Singapore Territorial Waters off Tuas.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: On 25 October 2018, Malaysia unilaterally extended the Johor Bahru Port Limits into Singapore Territorial Waters off Tuas.

sections.label: Singapore extends port limits off Tuas
sections.summary: On 6 December 2018, Singapore extended its own port limits off Tuas in response to Malaysia's provocative actions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: In response to Malaysia’s provocative actions, on 6 December 2018, we extended Singapore’s own port limits off Tuas.

sections.label: Working group on waters off Tuas
sections.summary: A working group headed by Chee Wee Kiong and Muhammad Shahrul Ikram Yaakob will discuss legal and operational matters to de-escalate the situation off Tuas.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: In summary, we agreed to establish a working group, headed by the Permanent Secretary of Singapore's Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) Mr Chee Wee Kiong and the Secretary General of the Malaysian Foreign Ministry Mr Muhammad Shahrul Ikram Yaakob.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: This working group will discuss both the legal and operational matters in order to de-escalate the situation in the waters off Tuas and they are to report to both Minister Saifuddin and me within the next two months.

sections.label: Singapore UNCLOS Article 298 declaration
sections.summary: Singapore filed a declaration under Article 298(1)(a) of UNCLOS on 12 December 2018, as dispute settlement should be on mutually agreed terms.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: However, the dispute settlement should be on terms that are mutually agreed to by both parties and it is for this reason that Singapore filed a declaration under Article 298(1)(a) of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS).

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We filed this declaration on 12 December 2018.

sections.label: ILS and Pasir Gudang development
sections.summary: The ILS imposes no additional requirements or limitations preventing Malaysia from developing tall buildings or operating tall ships in Pasir Gudang.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The ILS imposes no additional requirements or limitations preventing Malaysia from developing tall buildings in Pasir Gudang or operating tall ships in Pasir Gudang Port.

sections.label: Satellite photo of Pasir Gudang high-rises
sections.summary: A satellite photograph from open sources shows existing high-rise developments in Pasir Gudang, so the ILS has not and will not prevent tall structures.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: You can see from the satellite photograph – which I want to emphasise was obtained from open sources – that there are, indeed, existing high-rise developments in the Pasir Gudang area.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: So, the ILS has not and will not prevent the building of tall structures, as alleged by Malaysia.

sections.label: Malaysia NOTAMs over Pasir Gudang
sections.summary: A NOTAM was cancelled on 20 December 2018, but on 25 December 2018 CAAM issued another declaring a permanent Restricted Area over Pasir Gudang from 2 January 2019.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: This NOTAM was subsequently cancelled on 20 December 2018.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But, subsequently, on Christmas Day, 25 December 2018, CAAM issued another NOTAM, this time, declaring a permanent Restricted Area over Pasir Gudang between 2,000 feet and 5,000 feet altitude, for "military activities" and that this Restricted Area would take effect from 2 January 2019.

sections.label: Mutual suspension of ILS and Restricted Area
sections.summary: Singapore and Malaysia agreed to suspend the ILS procedures at Seletar Airport and the permanent Restricted Area for one month, effective midnight on 9 January 2019.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: At our meeting last week, Minister Saifuddin and I agreed that Singapore would suspend the implementation of the ILS procedures at Seletar Airport, and Malaysia would also suspend the permanent Restricted Area, for a period of one month in the first instance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: This mutual suspension went into effect simultaneously at midnight on 9 January 2019 and this has allowed normal operations to resume at Seletar Airport, with aircraft able to fly their normal established flight paths over Pasir Gudang in and out of Seletar.

sections.label: 1962 Water Agreement price discussions
sections.summary: Both Prime Ministers agreed the two Attorneys-General would meet to discuss whether Malaysia still had the right to review the water price under the 1962 Water Agreement.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Another matter that Malaysia has raised is the price of raw water sold to Singapore under the 1962 Water Agreement.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Both Prime Ministers agreed that the two Attorneys-General respectively would meet for discussions to better understand each other’s positions on whether Malaysia still had the right to review the price of water under the 1962 Water Agreement.

sections.label: Johor Menteri Besar vessel visit
sections.summary: The Menteri Besar's publicised visit to a Malaysian vessel in Singapore waters made the JMC meeting untenable, so Singapore protested and proposed postponing it.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: This meeting would have involved Singapore and Malaysian Ministers and officials, as well as Johor officials, including the Menteri Besar Osman Sapian.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But most regrettably, the Menteri Besar staged a publicised visit to the Malaysian Marine Department (MMD) vessel anchored in Singapore Territorial Waters off Tuas on 9 January 2019.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: It undermined the goodwill and trust that are necessary for further cooperation between the two countries, and especially cooperation involving Johor.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Therefore, it made it untenable for us to proceed with the JMC meeting this morning.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Singapore formally protested the intrusion via a TPN, a diplomatic note, to Malaysia, and we proposed to postpone the meeting to a later date.

sections.label: Khaw and Loke meeting
sections.summary: Minister Khaw and Minister Loke are due to meet, hopefully by the end of this month.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: What I will state is Minister Khaw and Minister Loke are due to meet, hopefully, by the end of this month.

sections.label: Actions protect sovereignty, negotiations needed
sections.summary: Current actions protect and assert sovereignty and sovereign rights, and negotiations are needed to resolve the issues through frank exchange.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Well, first of all, our current actions are designed precisely to protect and assert our sovereignty and our sovereign rights.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We do need negotiations to resolve these issues.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I believe these issues are solvable, but it needs to be a frank, open, candid, sincere exchange of views.

sections.label: Ministers Saifuddin and Azmin found sincere
sections.summary: In all interactions with Minister Saifuddin and Minister Azmin, the speaker found them sincere, constructive and helpful, and believes both.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Specifically, to the Member's question, I can quite confidently state for the record that in all my interactions with Minister Saifuddin and Minister Azmin, I have found them to be sincere, constructive, helpful, and I believe both of them.

sections.label: Personal ties not replacement for interests
sections.summary: For the two interacted with most intensively the answer is yes, but personal ties cannot replace national interests, international law or agreements.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But my short answer to the Member is that as far as the two whom I have interacted most intensively with, the answer is yes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But never, never make the mistake of assuming that personal ties can be a replacement for national interests, international law or complying with agreements.

sections.label: De-escalation commitment then vessels entered
sections.summary: After the 8 January 2019 meeting with Minister Saifuddin there was a commitment to de-escalate, yet less than two days later five vessels came into our waters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Minister, I applaud Singapore's approach in taking a calm, sensible approach to the problems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But one of the things that causes me great concern is that there definitely have been very constructive sounds coming out of MFA, and after the meeting on 8 January 2019 with Minister Saifuddin, there was a commitment to de-escalate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Yet, less than two days after that, five vessels came into our waters.

sections.label: Johor Menteri Besar intrusion response
sections.summary: Singapore postponed the 14th Joint Ministerial Committee for Iskandar Malaysia after the Johor Menteri Besar's intrusion, and will take measures to safeguard its interests.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: In the case of the recent intrusion by the Johor Menteri Besar, in fact, he did that the day after the bilateral meeting with Foreign Minister Saifuddin, and as I said just now, is completely against the spirit of the meeting and against the spirit of the agreements.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: No, the answer is we cannot just let it pass.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: That is why we had to postpone the meeting of the 14th Joint Ministerial Committee for Iskandar Malaysia.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: So, my point is, do not take Singapore's consistency, and some would say even predictability, for granted.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We will always take appropriate measures to safeguard our interests, and any country dealing with Singapore must not assume that it is cost-free to embark on any adventures or antics against us.

sections.label: Additional treated water to Johor
sections.summary: Singapore supplied an additional six million gallons per day of treated water to Johor state last week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Indeed, Singapore more than honoured our agreements on many occasions; just last week, we supplied an additional six million gallons per day (mgd) of treated water to Johor state.

sections.label: 1962 Water Agreement sacrosanct
sections.summary: Singapore regards the 1962 Water Agreement as sacrosanct.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: To us, the 1962 Water Agreement is sacrosanct.

sections.label: Water volumes and subsidised pricing
sections.summary: Singapore honours agreements, is obliged to sell only five mgd but supplies 16 mgd, and prices additional treated water at 50 sen per 1,000 gallons.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But even beyond that, beyond Independence, it is a foundational principle of Singapore's operating system, that we fully honour all agreements that we enter into.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Now, specifically for water, apart from the issue of the price of raw water and the price of treated water, which are stipulated in the agreement, the volume of water that Singapore is obliged to sell to Malaysia, in fact, is only five mgd, strictly speaking, 2% of 250 mgd.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But the Member has quite rightly pointed out that, actually, in practice, for quite some time and, in fact, if you ask Minister Masagos today how much water he is supplying to Malaysia, he will tell you 16 mgd.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We do not do it because of an imposition from the Water Agreement.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: And out of goodwill, we have also priced the additional treated water at 50 sen per 1,000 gallons, which everyone knows is a subsidised price.
